we present a novel immunohistochemical approach to detect several beta-amyloids in one and the same senile plaque, which may contribute to a better understanding of the pathomechanisms in Alzheimer's disease.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

beta-amyloid deposits in Alzheimer's disease, monkeys and mice are not composed of a single beta-amyloid isoform but rather of several beta-isoforms with different amino acid endings and/or amino-terminal truncations.

the concomitant detection of beta-amyloids with N-terminal truncations and different C-terminal ends is possible by triple immunofluo- rescence labelling and that this approach can be used to study the distribution of beta-amy- loids in the human brain, in non-human primates, and in transgenic mice.

beta-amyloid pE3-x and beta-amyloid 42 are the most important beta-amyloid components in cortical plaques of Alzheimer's disease, and that beta-amyloids 40 and pE3-x are the major beta-amyloid constituents in the vascular amyloid of these brains.

the concomitant detection of different beta-amyloid peptide forms in senile plaques may help to understand their pathogenic role in Alzheimer's disease.
